title: 1957 AHSME Problem 44
statement: In triangle \(ABC,\) \(AC=CD\) and \(\angle CAB-\angle ABC=30^\circ.\) Then \(\angle BAD\) is:

solutions.text:
Let \(\alpha=\angle CAB,\) \(\beta=\angle ABC,\) and \(x=\angle BAD.\) Since \(D\) lies on \(BC,\) \[ \angle ADC=x+\beta \] as an exterior angle of triangle \(ABD.\) Because \(AC=CD,\) triangle \(ACD\) is isosceles, so \(\angle CAD=\angle ADC.\) But \(\angle CAD=\alpha-x.\) Hence \[ \alpha-x=x+\beta, \] so \(2x=\alpha-\beta=30^\circ\) and \(x=15^\circ.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
